column1: # TITLE: EGFR-mediated FASN signaling promotes TKI resistant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer tumor cell survival
# SUMMARY: Metabolic reprogramming is widely known as a hallmark of cancer cells to allow adaptation of cells to sustain survival signals. In the past decade
column2: altered lipid metabolism has been recognized to be a property of malignant cells. In this report
column3: we describe a novel oncogenic signaling pathway exclusively in tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-resistant epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). EGFR mediates TKI-resistance through regulation of the fatty acid synthase (FASN)
column4: and inhibition of this pathway using the FASN inhibitor Orlistat
column5: triggers cell death and reduces tumor sizes both in culture systems and in vivo. Together
column6: data shown here provide compelling evidence that the fatty acid metabolism pathway is a candidate target for TKI-resistant NSCLC treatment.
